title: Express operations with direct verbs
text: When editable prose describes an action, use a direct verb permitted for that meaning and context if it is clearer than a nominalization or a support-verb phrase. Replace wording such as perform a validation with the corresponding direct action only when the actor, object, timing, modality, and effect remain the same. Rebuild the sentence as needed rather than mechanically exchange words. Keep a noun when it names a concept, state, result, interface element, or machine-significant entity instead of hiding an action. If no applicable verb entry exists, request lexical review; do not turn an admitted noun into a verb solely to shorten the sentence.
exceptions: A concept such as authentication or a result such as a validation report can be the actual subject of discussion. Do not force every action-related noun into a verb.
Commands, fields, interface labels, and quoted strings retain their exact noun or verb wording. Give a direct surrounding instruction without renaming the element.
A shorter verb must not change a verification into a repair, a permission into a command, or an automatic operation into a reader step. Example verbs are not global lexical approvals.

segments.text: Before the deployment starts, validate the configuration.

allowed.rationale: In a context where validate is admitted for this check, the direct verb replaces Perform a validation of the configuration without changing the prerequisite.
The surrounding action is direct, while the interface label and report concept remain nouns. The label is illustrative, not an actual product specification.

segments.text: Perform the execution of a validation of the configuration before the deployment starts.

not_allowed.rationale: In the same intended context as the positive example, the support-verb chain hides the operation. Use the direct validation verb and keep the timing condition.
The rule does not prohibit concept nouns or authorize changing a fixed interface label. Keep the label and express the reader action outside it.

facets.source_facet: A permitted verb can express an action more directly than noun-based wording.
facets.rationale: Prefer an applicable IT verb while retaining genuine concepts and exact external names; do not infer verb admission from a noun.

criteria: Confirm that the direct verb has an applicable lexical entry and preserves actor, object, timing, obligation, and operation; this pilot supplies no vocabulary.
Distinguish a hidden operation from a concept or result noun and verify the fictional Validation label stays literal.
Check that a direct rewrite does not imply permission to rename an interface or replace validation with correction.

Review every allocated Issue 9 source block at its recorded physical PDF pages for semantic facet completeness and distinguish retained principles from IT-specific changes; locator coverage alone is insufficient.

Check original English wording, example judgments, exceptions, domain scope, literal boundaries and digests, and the unchanged original-content rights and attribution. Examples do not admit vocabulary; supporting IDs are planned references, not canonical endpoints or delegated provenance.

Preserve technical meaning, actors, modality, branch conditions, limits, and required safety and security context. Escalate unresolved external-requirement conflicts rather than silently rewrite. Human review remains necessary: structural validation neither approves nor releases this draft or makes it official ASD guidance.
